state_vocabulary.layering_rule: A mechanism BLOCKED never becomes an experiment BLOCKED automatically. Experiment BLOCKED means only that the bench could not establish or complete the preregistered scenario.

C4.name: root_has_no_preexisting_children
C4.defect_when: exists process with ppid == root.pid at S0 time

C7.name: sigchld_disposition_default
C7.defect_when: SIGCHLD ignored (getsignal != SIG_DFL or /proc/self/status SigIgn bit 16 set)

proof_rules.PR-S0-1: Proves 'root leads its own session': the kernel-reported sid of the registered root equals its pid. Premise: root fingerprint verified (pid,starttime) before the read.
proof_rules.PR-S0-2: Proves 'root session differs from the supervisor session': root.sid != os.getsid(0) of the supervisor process.
proof_rules.PR-S0-3: Proves 'root leads its process group': root.pgrp == root.pid.
proof_rules.PR-S0-4: Proves 'root has no children at S0 time': a complete /proc enumeration (no unreadable entry, no ScanFailed) finds no process with ppid == root.pid.
proof_rules.PR-S0-5: Proves 'the supervisor has no children other than the root and its declared auxiliaries': complete /proc enumeration of ppid == supervisor pid.
proof_rules.PR-S0-6: Proves 'the registered fingerprint still describes the live root': re-read (pid,starttime,sid,pgrp) equals the registered tuple.
proof_rules.PR-S0-7: Proves 'SIGCHLD is not ignored': signal.getsignal(SIGCHLD) is SIG_DFL and the SigIgn bit for signal 17 in /proc/self/status is clear.
proof_rules.PR-S0-8: Proves 'the subreaper flag is set': prctl set returned success AND prctl get returned 1.

P0.label: original CA/CB preflight (CPU-001 a_lab.ArmCA)
P0.ecd_note: register_root() compares the live /proc fingerprint with the supplied node record (-> PR-S0-6); preflight() sets and reads back the subreaper flag (-> PR-S0-8). There is no session, process-group, children or SIGCHLD check. ES-CW (closed-world declaration) and ES-SID (sid_hint without S0 session verification) are NOT proofs.
P0.adapter: a_lab.Blocked raised by register_root -> BLOCKED(ROOT_FINGERPRINT_MISMATCH); preflight() status BLOCKED -> BLOCKED(PREFLIGHT_FAILED); otherwise ACCEPT.

P1.label: strict variant preflight (CPU-002 e2_lab.ArmCAS)
P1.ecd_note: As P0 plus StrictMixin.preflight(): dedicated_session = (root.sid == root.pid) and (root.sid != os.getsid(0)), reported as the single code STAGE_SESSION_NOT_DEDICATED (it cannot tell C1 from C2). PR-S0-3 is implied by C1 only when C1 holds. No children or SIGCHLD checks.
P1.adapter: As P0; status BLOCKED with code STAGE_SESSION_NOT_DEDICATED is reported as is.

P2.label: S0 candidate s0_check() (O-2 definition; new bench code)
P2.ecd_note: All eight direct kernel-read checks; every failing check yields its own code and the full set is reported (sorted).
P2.adapter: s0_check(view) returns ACCEPT with the list of evaluated rules, or BLOCKED with the sorted code set and cited rules.

P3.label: event stream (proc connector)
P3.note: Read-only feasibility investigation only (no system configuration change). Not declared PROVABLE for any E1-A scenario; no E1-A classification exists.

P4.label: cgroup membership
P4.note: Read-only feasibility investigation only; this environment has cgroup v1 controllers only. Not declared PROVABLE for any E1-A scenario; no E1-A classification exists.

refinements: Plan item (e) 'root already has unregistered children at S0' was ambiguous: split into E1A-e1 (root has a child) and E1A-e2 (supervisor has an undeclared child).
Plan item (h) covers two different failures (set fails / read-back mismatch): split into E1A-h1 and E1A-h2.

ERRATA-002 section 1.4 lumps (b)-(i) as 'misconfiguration, expect BLOCKED'. A bystander in the supervisor's session is harmless when the root is a correct dedicated session leader, so that situation is registered as the benign control E1A-a2 (expect ACCEPT); the dangerous combination remains E1A-i.
Plan item (d) 'root is not a process-group leader' cannot occur for a session leader; it is registered as a non-leader member of a different session.

E1A-a.description: Correct configuration: root is a fresh session leader (sid==pgid==pid), sid != supervisor sid; supervisor has exactly the root as child; SIGCHLD default; subreaper settable.
E1A-a.construction: SUP forks root via GATED-SPAWN; root calls setsid() after RELEASE.

E1A-a2.description: Benign control: correct root as in E1A-a, PLUS a non-child bystander X that shares the SUPERVISOR's session (S0 must not depend on the cleanliness of the supervisor's own session).
E1A-a2.construction: As E1A-a; during the SETUP phase, which precedes the candidate's S0 and runs BEFORE the subreaper flag is set (so X is re-parented away from SUP, not to it), the SUP stub forks node M via GATED-SPAWN; M forks X via GATED-SPAWN (X stays in the supervisor's session) and exits; the SUP stub reaps M by specific pid; X is verified by the observer to be a live non-child of SUP in the supervisor's session before S0 starts, otherwise the trial is bench-BLOCKED (TOPOLOGY_NOT_AS_DESIGNED).

E1A-b.description: Root shares the supervisor's session and process group (plain child).
E1A-b.construction: SUP forks root via GATED-SPAWN; root performs no setsid/setpgid.

E1A-c.description: Root has its own process group but the same session as the supervisor.
E1A-c.construction: SUP forks root; root calls setpgid(0,0) only.

E1A-d.description: Root is a non-leader member of a different session (sid != supervisor sid, sid != root pid, pgrp != root pid).
E1A-d.construction: SUP forks leader node L (L calls setsid()); L forks root via GATED-SPAWN; root performs no setsid/setpgid.

E1A-e1.description: Correct dedicated root, but root already has an unregistered child at S0 time.
E1A-e1.construction: As E1A-a; the root node spawns child via GATED-SPAWN before S0.

E1A-e2.description: Correct dedicated root, but the supervisor has an additional undeclared child Y at S0 time.
E1A-e2.construction: As E1A-a; SUP forks Y via GATED-SPAWN and does not declare it.

E1A-f.description: Registered root fingerprint no longer matches the live root (pid-reuse style staleness).
E1A-f.construction: As E1A-a; the registered starttime handed to the candidate is incremented by 1 (injection).

E1A-g.description: SIGCHLD is ignored in the supervisor (inherited SIG_IGN across exec).
E1A-g.construction: As E1A-a; the gated child sets SIGCHLD to SIG_IGN before exec'ing the supervisor stub, so the disposition is inherited.

E1A-h1.description: Subreaper flag cannot be set (prctl set returns failure).
E1A-h1.construction: As E1A-a; the candidate's prctl-set function is replaced by one that fails (injection).

E1A-h2.description: Subreaper flag read-back mismatch (prctl get returns 0 after a successful set).
E1A-h2.construction: As E1A-a; the candidate's prctl-get function is replaced by one that returns 0 (injection).

E1A-i.description: Dangerous topology of CPU-002 E1-S2: root shares the supervisor's session AND an unrelated non-child bystander X lives in that session.
E1A-i.construction: As E1A-b; additionally the same SETUP-phase M/X construction as in E1A-a2 (X orphaned into the supervisor's session before the subreaper flag is set).

classification_note: Classification is derived mechanically: a scenario with no defect is PROVABLE/ACCEPT; a scenario whose defects share no rule with the candidate's ECD is UNPROVABLE; otherwise PROVABLE with the code set the candidate can emit. P0 is a baseline: the frozen rule predicts FAIL for P0 wherever a scenario is UNPROVABLE for it and P0 answers ACCEPT; that is a consequence of its capability, not a number used to tune criteria. P3/P4 are not classified because their capability is unverified.
bench_unverifiable_conditions: scenario topology differs from the intended construction when read back from the kernel (TOPOLOGY_NOT_AS_DESIGNED)
lineage ledger record missing or incomplete for any node in the trial
blindness assertion fails (ledger path or role visible in the supervisor's argv/environment/open descriptors)
GATED-SPAWN bench validity check failed earlier in the same run

independent_truth.lifecycle_and_identity_stability: pidfd (readability) + /proc stat + waitid(WNOWAIT) for direct children; at least two sources must agree. pidfd is NEVER used to infer lineage.
independent_truth.ownership_lineage: Lineage ledger created by the observer at GATED-SPAWN registration: node id, creator, role, creation sequence, birth (pid, starttime), session_mode. The supervisor under test is blind to it.
independent_truth.kernel_configuration_readback: Observer reads /proc/<root>/stat (sid, pgrp), /proc/<supervisor>/stat (sid), enumerates ppid relations, reads /proc/<supervisor>/status SigIgn; the subreaper flag is read by a bench stub inside the supervisor process, independent of the candidate's own call.
independent_truth.danger_oracle: Signals and waits attempted by the supervisor are recorded by instrumentation wrappers; non-target liveness is read from pidfd + /proc. /proc fields being equal is never treated as identity proof.

order: 1. If any bench_unverifiable condition holds or the bench raised -> BLOCKED (bench).

2. If any unsafe event occurred (any signal, kill or wait call issued by the candidate between the start of preflight and the S0 verdict; any signal delivered to a process not in the trial's own target set; a wait call on a pid that is not a direct child of the supervisor; a non-target process killed or no longer alive at the end of the trial) -> FAIL (safety), regardless of anything else. E1-A judges only the S0 verdict and its side-effect freedom; downstream attribution harm is E1-B/C/D scope.
3. class PROVABLE and expected ACCEPT: PASS iff s0_verdict == ACCEPT; BLOCKED -> FAIL (false reject, availability); UNKNOWN -> FAIL.

4. class PROVABLE and expected BLOCKED: PASS iff s0_verdict == BLOCKED and the reported code set equals expected_codes exactly and the cited rules include cited_rules_required and are within the ECD and no signal/wait occurred before the verdict; otherwise FAIL.
5. class UNPROVABLE (expected REFUSE_ANY): PASS iff s0_verdict is BLOCKED (any codes) or UNKNOWN; ACCEPT -> FAIL even if the scenario happened to be harmless.

6. Cell verdict: PASS iff every repetition PASS; any FAIL -> FAIL (unstable results are FAIL); bench-BLOCKED repetitions are excluded from the cell numerator and denominator but reported; if bench-BLOCKED exceeds 5% of the planned repetitions the cell is INSUFFICIENT and the experiment verdict for that cell is BLOCKED.
7. Exclusion of repetitions is decided only from bench-level causes, never from the mechanism output; a BLOCKED repetition may be re-run under unchanged code; both records are kept.
verdict_function.first_action_order_check: The sequence numbers in the supervisor event log must show S0_VERDICT before any SIGNAL or WAIT event (bench-infrastructure waits on M by pid are labelled and excluded).

repetitions.false_reject_sweep: E1A-a x {P1,P2} x launch contexts {L1,L2,L3,L4} x 50 trials

launch_contexts.L1: supervisor is a fresh session leader
launch_contexts.L4: L1 with a controlling terminal (pty); bench-BLOCKED if no pty is available

repetitions.note: No count proves the absence of races; E1-A scenarios are deterministic constructions.

checks.BV-1: An unreleased gated process executes no experiment action while the observer is alive and withholds RELEASE.
checks.BV-2: If the observer is killed before REGISTERED is written, the gated process exits by itself (EOF) within T_gate_max and no unregistered process remains.
checks.BV-3: A gated process exits by itself when the gate stays silent for T_gate_max.
checks.BV-4: For every released node, the REGISTERED line precedes the RELEASE byte (checked from REG order and recorded sequence numbers).
checks.BV-5: Descendants created by released nodes follow the same ticket/gate protocol; a node cannot release its own child.
checks.BV-6: The janitor refuses to signal when the re-opened pidfd's process has a different starttime than the record.
checks.BV-7: The janitor ignores INTENT-only records and a torn (newline-less) last REG line.
checks.BV-8: No gate write end is open in any child after the child's first fd-hygiene step (checked from /proc/<pid>/fd).
checks.BV-9: Blindness: the supervisor stub's argv, environment and open file descriptors contain neither the ledger/REG path nor any role label.
checks.BV-10: Instrumentation wrappers for os.kill, os.killpg, signal.pidfd_send_signal, os.waitpid and os.waitid are installed in the supervisor stub before any candidate code is imported.

pass_fail_blocked.PASS: per verdict_function steps 3-5 and 6 for every cell, all bench validity checks passed, zero unsafe events, evidence complete.
pass_fail_blocked.FAIL: any unsafe event; any cell FAIL; any unstable cell.
pass_fail_blocked.BLOCKED: bench validity check failed; bench-unverifiable condition; INSUFFICIENT cell; cleanup failure (identity not confirmable); capability missing.

safety_boundaries: only bench-created sacrificial processes; every one created through GATED-SPAWN
the supervisor stub runs in a fresh session created by the bench
signals only to registered processes after re-verifying (pid, starttime), via pidfd opened first
no pkill, no name matching, no process-group cleanup, no kill -- -pgid, no cleanup killpg
command-line tokens are diagnostic only and never authorize a signal
no GPU, no network, no real data, no system configuration change
cleanup_procedure: observer: re-verify registered (pid, starttime) against /proc, then pidfd_send_signal(SIGKILL) to still-running registered nodes, waitpid by specific pid for own children
if the observer dies: janitor reads REG, acts only on INTENT + complete REGISTERED records, re-opens pidfd first and then compares starttime
residual check by registry; token scan is a diagnostic report only; any identity that cannot be confirmed -> no signal, record, trial BLOCKED, next trial not started
evidence_outputs: per-trial JSON: scenario, candidate, repetition, launch context, environment, git commit/status, prereg sha256, class, mechanism output (verdict, codes, cited rules, event log), instrumentation log, truth readback, lineage ledger excerpt, danger-oracle result, verdict and reasons, evidence_kind
final integrity verification (git ls-files and remote tree check performed after commit)
evidence_path_rules: Evidence directories must avoid names matched by the repository .gitignore (parts/, *_archive, *.log, dist/, lib/, var/, downloads/). git check-ignore must be run before the first run and the remote tree must be verified after pushing.
known_limitations: E1-A tests the S0 verdict, not the later attribution quality (E1-B/C/D).
same-uid blindness is by construction, not a security boundary
scenarios f, h1, h2 are SIMULATED injections
P3/P4 are unverified capabilities and are not evaluated here
design correctness is not run correctness: nothing in this file has been executed
amendment_policy: No change after the first run of any cell. A later fix is a new file e1_provability_table_v2.json; v1 and every result obtained under v1 are retained, and affected cells are re-run under v2.
